bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470156 (gnutls): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470156
bug_description.normalized: The saved 13-byte DER witness is accepted far enough as a PKCS#12 PFX for `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` to inspect `authSafe.contentType`. In the vulnerable helper, stack buffer `oid` is declared without initialization and then passed to `asn1_read_value(pkcs12, "authSafe.contentType", oid, &len)`. The witness encodes that field as the one-byte OID payload `06 01 20`, so only a short textual OID is written into the front of `oid`; the rest of the 128-byte stack buffer stays indeterminate. The subsequent `strcmp(oid, DATA_OID)` is observed by MemorySanitizer as a 21-byte `__interceptor_memcmp` read, matching the 20-byte literal `"1.2.840.113549.1.7.1"` plus NUL, and the first poisoned byte appears at offset 5. MemorySanitizer attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of `oid` in `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that materializes the vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled field into local state by reading the parsed PKCS#12 `authSafe.contentType` OID into stack buffer `oid`.
source.value_from: The staged witness bytes are `30 0b 02 00 30 07 06 01 20 a0 01 20 ff` (hex). The `06 01 20` subfield is the attacker-controlled `authSafe.contentType` OID that this call converts into a short textual string in `oid`.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The fixed-string comparison on `DATA_OID` consumes bytes from stack `oid` that were never initialized by the earlier short OID read.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 5 inside [oid, 21)` and then `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at this line.

root_cause.description: The local OID buffer is allocated on the stack without initialization even though later logic compares it against a fixed 21-byte string after only partially populating it from attacker-controlled input.
root_cause.note: No zero-fill occurs before `asn1_read_value` writes the short `authSafe.contentType` string. Bytes in `oid` beyond that short prefix remain indeterminate and are later consumed by `strcmp(oid, DATA_OID)`.

parser_admitted.condition: The saved crash proves the witness passes this DER import step and later reaches `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` -> `gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag` -> `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Earliest project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled 13-byte witness into the internal ASN.1 PKCS#12 object later queried on the crashing path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The fuzz harness passes the staged 13-byte file `poc` as `raw = {data, size}` to `gnutls_pkcs12_import`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Later `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` reads `authSafe.contentType` out of this imported ASN.1 object.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness imports the 13-byte witness as DER PKCS#12 and then calls `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` on the resulting object.
DER-decodes the attacker-controlled bytes into `pkcs12->pkcs12`, making the `authSafe.contentType` field available to later helper reads.
Starts iterating bags in the imported PKCS#12 object and requests bag 0 through `gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag`.
Calls `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` to decode the top-level authenticated safe before inspecting bag content types.
Reads the witness's short `authSafe.contentType` OID into an uninitialized stack buffer and then compares 21 bytes against `DATA_OID`, triggering the saved MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Allocates the stack buffer that will hold the textual `authSafe.contentType` OID without initializing any of its 128 bytes. The saved MSAN trace attributes the poisoned value to this stack allocation in `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`.

Source step. The helper reads the attacker-controlled `authSafe.contentType` OID from the imported PKCS#12 object into `oid` and continues only because `result == ASN1_SUCCESS`. The witness encodes this field as `06 01 20`, so only a short textual OID is written into the front of `oid`; MSAN's first poisoned byte at offset 5 shows the remaining bytes of the stack buffer stay uninitialized.

MSAN sink. No initialization or exact-length guard precedes this fixed-string comparison. `DATA_OID` is `"1.2.840.113549.1.7.1"` (20 characters plus NUL), and the saved trace shows this compare as a 21-byte `__interceptor_memcmp` read from `oid`. Because step 2 defined only the short OID prefix, the compare consumes uninitialized tail bytes and aborts here.

allocation_context.note: The saved trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `oid` in the stack frame of `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe`; the actual declaration is line 53.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and the provided `fixed_commit` do not modify `lib/x509/pkcs12.c` or this call path, so they do not substantiate the fix for the witnessed crash.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is the 13-byte DER blob `30 0b 02 00 30 07 06 01 20 a0 01 20 ff`. The saved reproduction proves it imports far enough as PKCS#12 for `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` to read `authSafe.contentType`; that field is encoded by the short OID payload `06 01 20`, and the later fixed-string compare on `DATA_OID` triggers the saved MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value at `lib/x509/pkcs12.c:67`.

format.name: PKCS#12 DER
format.contract: The available evidence establishes only the exact 13-byte DER blob `30 0b 02 00 30 07 06 01 20 a0 01 20 ff` (hex). In the saved run, this blob is accepted far enough as a PKCS#12 PFX for `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` to read the short `authSafe.contentType` OID encoded by `06 01 20` into stack `oid` and then compare 21 bytes against `DATA_OID`, reaching uninitialized bytes at offset 5. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader PKCS#12 input class.
